column2: That pressed bull Soma flows in the filter for drinking, smiting demons, god-seeking.
That all-seeing bay one flows in the filter, the sustainer, roaring toward his nest.
That racer, flowing, runs through the lights of heaven, demon-slayer, to the woolen sieve.
He, flowing, made the sun shine on the heights of Trita, together with the sisters.
That Vritra-slayer, bull, pressed, finder of room, unconquerable, Soma, runs like strength.
That god, urged by the seer, runs to the vessels, the drop glorifying Indra.
Whoever studies the Pavamani verses, the essence gathered by the sages, eats all that is purified, sweetened by Matarishvan.
To him who studies the Pavamani verses, the essence gathered by sages, Sarasvati yields milk, ghee, honey and water.
The Pavamani verses bring welfare, good milkers, ghee-dripping; the essence gathered by the sages is placed among the Brahmins as immortality.
May the Pavamanis support us in this world and the next; may the goddesses, brought together with the gods, fulfill our desires.
By the filter with which the gods ever purify themselves, by that thousand-streamed one may the Pavamanis purify us.
By the Pavamanis, bringers of welfare, he goes to joy; he enjoys pure foods and attains immortality.
With great homage we have approached the youngest, who shone kindled in his own house — of wondrous splendor, between the wide worlds, well offered, facing all sides.
He, overcoming all evils by his greatness, Agni, I praise in the house, Jatavedas; may he protect us from evil and blame, us who sing and our bounteous ones.
You, Agni, are Varuna and Mitra; the Vasishthas strengthen you with thoughts; in you may be good wealth; protect us always with blessings.
Great is Indra, who by strength, like rain-bringing Parjanya, has grown by the hymns of Vatsa.
When the Kanvas made Indra the accomplisher of the sacrifice with hymns, they speak their weapons as kin.
When the carriers bear the offspring of truth, the sages carry along the truth.
The shining, swift drops of the flowing slayer, the bay one, have been released, with ageless flame.
Flowing, the best charioteer, with bright ones the most glorious in praise, the golden-bay with the Marut host.
Flowing one, pervade with your rays, best winner of strength, giving heroic vigor to the praiser.
Now purified by the wool, flow around, unharmed, most fragrant; at the pressing, in the waters, we rejoice with the drink, mixing with cows for the higher.
Sounding around for seeing, delight of the gods, the skill, the drop, the all-seeing.
Parjanya, father of the great winged one, holds a dwelling on the navel of earth in the mountains; the sister waters flow toward the cows; with stones he dwells at the rite of the feast.
The seer goes around the great one by the ordainer's way; like a horse cleansed, you go toward strength; driving away evils, Soma, be gracious to us; clad in ghee, you go to the cleansing.
Praise the unwearying giver, the giver of wealth; Indra's gifts are good; he who is not angered by the wish of the one who serves him, urging his mind to give.
From whatever, Indra, we fear, from that make us safe; bounteous one, help us for our protection; drive away foes and enemies.
You, lord of bounty, are the upholder of great bounty and dwelling; we, O bounteous Indra, lover of songs, having pressed, call you.
You, Soma, are holding, joyful, most vigorous at the sacrifice; flow, wealth magnifying.
You, pressed, most exhilarating, vigorous, most joyful drop, ever-victorious, unconquered.
You, pressed by stones, flow roaring; bring splendid strength.
Your drops, water-leaping, grew Indra for exhilaration; the gods drank you for immortality.
Run to us, pressed, purifying drops, bringing wealth, the rain-giving, flowing waters, finders of heaven.
Whom the friends, twice five, of self-glory, united with the stone; the waves cleanse Indra's dear, desirable one.
For Indra, to drink, Soma, you are sprinkled around — for the Vritra-slayer, the man, and the hero who gives gifts, sitting in the seat.
The pressers cleanse for exhilaration your essence, the soma, for great splendor.
They cleanse the newborn bay child, soma, the drop in the filter for the gods.
Let our songs strengthen him, like women the calf — who is the heart's gift of Indra.
Flow for us, Soma, welfare for the cow; milk the swelling nourishment; strengthen the praiseworthy ocean.
Great is the fuel of those, abundant the praise, wide the sound, of whom Indra is the youthful friend.
The hero goes among the troops with the unfought, surrounded by fighters, of whom Indra is the youthful friend.
He who alone distributes wealth to the giving mortal, the ruler, not to be gainsaid — indeed Indra.
Whoever, for many, serves you after pressing, that fierce strength lords — indeed Indra.
When will he crush the ungenerous mortal under foot like a mushroom? When will Indra hear our songs?
When he climbs from peak to peak, much must be done; Indra perceives the aim; the bull stirs with his herd.
Yoke your two long-maned bay horses, fertile and filling the girths; then, O soma-drinking Indra, come to hear our songs.
Kindled well, bring the gods for the offerer, O priest, O purifier; and worship.
Honeyed, O Tanunapat, make our sacrifice among the gods, O seer; today do it for the call.
I call here the dear Narashamsa to this sacrifice, honey-tongued, offering-maker.
O Agni, in your most comfortable chariot, praised, bring the gods; you are the priest set by Manu.
Today at the sun's rising may sinless Mitra, Aryaman, Savitar and Bhaga bring forth.
May that dwelling be well protected, and the good givers speedily go, who help us across sin.
And the self-rulers, Aditi, and those of the unharmed law, great kings, rule.
May the soma-drops delight you; make us rich, O stone-bearer; strike down the haters of prayer.
Press down with your foot the ungenerous Panis; you are great; for none is equal to you.
You rule the pressed and the unpressed, Indra; you are king of the peoples.
The wakeful sage of the thoughts of truth, Soma, flowing, sat in the vessels; to whom the pairs, the desirous, the Adhvaryus, the charioteers of fair hands, offer service.
He, purifying, placing near the sun in the fleece, filled heaven and earth, wide; whose dear helpers, dearly gained, never withhold the wealth from the doer.
He the increaser, the strengthener, flowing, Soma the bountiful, has helped us with light; where our ancient fathers, knowing the step, finders of heaven, sought the cattle and the rock.
Not bending, the bull swift like a cow, overcoming men; hateful, desirable, doing both, the greatest, with both.
These sweetest songs and hymns of praise rise up — victory-winning, wealth-giving, unfailing helpers, striving like chariots.
Like the Kanvas and the Bhrigus, like suns, they obtained all that thought desired; the Ayus, glorifying Indra with hymns, the Priyamedhas sounded.
You have brought forth the sun, flowing one, and in the rite by skill the milk; rushing with cow-quickening thought.
Thus for the immortal great dwelling, flow bright, divine, nectar.
May Indra drink of your pressed soma for skill and strength, and all the gods.
Like the sun's rays, the quickening, exhilarating ones, pressed forth, are sent together; the swift ones spread around the stretched thread; nothing flows to its abode without Indra.
The thought is mingled, honey is poured; the joyful one is urged within the mouth; the flowing continuous one, like the pressers', honeyed drop flows toward the sheep's wool.
The bull measures out, the cows go to meet him; they go to the divine one's appointed place; he passed beyond the white woolen sieve, Soma purified as a cleansed cloth.
Men with their fingers bring forth Agni from the two fire-sticks, the praised one released from the hand, the far-seeing lord of the house.
That Agni the Vasus set down at the dwelling, well seen, for help from anywhere — the skilful one, who was ever in the house.
Kindled, Agni, shine in front of us with ceaseless flame, O youngest; to you the eternal strengths come.
The thirty-seat abode shines; speech is set for the bird; in front of the dwelling by days.
Approaching the sacrifice, let us speak a mantra to Agni, who hears both near and far.
Who was first among the loving, the united peoples — he protected the house for the giver.
May the most comfortable Agni protect our wealth in the house, and guard us from distress.
Let the creatures also say: Agni, the Vritra-slayer, has been born, the winner of wealth in battle after battle.
Come to us, bring to the feast the offerings, bring the gods to drink the soma.
Arise, Agni, Bharata, shine brilliantly with ceaseless light; blaze, shine, ageless one.
Let the mortal not desire that speech of the pressed stalk; drive away the grudging dog, as the Bhrigus smote the sacrifice-spoiler.
The kinsman has come to the dwelling like a child to be nourished in the two enclosures; like a lover to a woman, like a bridegroom to the home.
That hero, accomplisher of skill, who propped heaven and earth, the bay one in the filter, the ordainer sitting in his seat.
You find no wealthy man for friendship; your horses drink well; when you make the sound, then you are invoked like a father.
May your two bay horses with peacock plumes, dun-backed, carry you in the golden chariot to drink the honeyed, enjoyed drink.
Drink of this pressed soma, lover of songs, like the first drinkers; this pouring of the adorned, juicy one goes for exhilaration, lovely.
The thousand-streamed bull, milking milk, dear to the god at his birth, who, born by truth, grew by truth; king, god, the great truth.
In the mother's womb, father of the father, shining in the imperishable, sitting in the seat of truth.
Bring a prayer with offspring, Jatavedas, all-seeing, Agni, who shine in heaven.
Clothing himself with auspicious garments, the great seer, speaking words, be proclaimed, purified in the vessels, all-seeing, wakeful at the gods' feast.
The dear one is cleansed on the woolen ridge, the most famous of the famed, the dweller with us; sound, bow, being purified; protect us always with blessings.
Come to us pure, Indra, pure with pure helps; pure, bestow wealth; pure, rejoice, soma-drinker.
Pure, Indra, give us wealth; pure, give jewels to the giver; pure, you slay Vritras; pure, you seek strength.
Agni, we think of the hymn, the effective one, today, touching heaven, we who seek the god's wealth.
May Agni accept our songs — the priest among men; may he worship the divine host.
You, Agni, are wide, welcomed, the choice priest; by you they extend the sacrifice.
The troop of heroes, with all heroes, strong, victorious, flow as winner of wealth; sharp-armed, swift-bowed, unconquerable in battles, overcoming foes in armies.
Wide-pastured, making fearless, flow together to the two, O plentiful; seeking waters, dawns, heaven and cattle, roar greatly to bring us strength.
Him indeed, now, O lord, the wise, we ask for bounty as a share; like a great protective hide are your shelters, Indra; may your favors reach us.
Agni, the grandson of the waters, fortunate, well-shining, of best flame; may he give us the favor of Mitra and Varuna and of the waters in heaven.
The mortal, O Agni, whom you aid in battles, whom you urge in contests — he restrains eternal strengths.
None overcomes his going around of any; strength is praiseworthy.
May he, all-seeing, be crossing strength with horses; may he be a winner with the sages.
Like a child longing with his mothers, the bull is held by the waters, much-chosen; like a man to a woman he goes to the appointed place; he joins the vessel with the milk.
The udder of the cow has swelled; the drop with streams joins the wise; the cows with milk in the vessels mix at the head, with bright garments.
May we be in your favor, O racer; do not cast us down to the enemy; protect us with wondrous helps, bring us to your good fortunes.
He, enjoying the lovely immortality, shook both heaven and earth with poetry; the sharpest waters surrounded him by greatness when they knew the seat by the god's fame.
May these banners of his be immortal, unconquerable, following both births; by which he purifies manly and divine strengths and then the kings grasp him with thought.
Flow toward Vayu for the feast, praised; toward Mitra and Varuna, purified; toward the man swift as thought, standing on the chariot; toward Indra, the bull, with thunderbolt in his arms.
Flow toward fair garments, toward good-milking cows, purified; toward shining gold for our bearing, toward horses and chariot-warriors, god Soma.
Flow to us toward heavenly treasures, toward all earthly ones, purified; flow to us by which we may gain wealth, the Arsheya, like Jamadagni.
From that the sacrifice was born, from that the hymn and the sound; you overcome all that is born and that will be born.
